subject: Agriculture
title: Fungi: The Silent Killers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fungi: The Silent Killers usable.

hook.text: Fungi cause 80% of all plant diseases. They rot, wilt, rust, and blight everything from wheat to bananas.

buildup.text: Fungal spores travel on wind, water, and soil. They can survive dormant for years waiting for the right host.

discovery.text: Wheat rust—a fungus—can devastate entire regions in a single growing season if resistant varieties aren't planted.

twist.text: A new wheat rust strain called Ug99 appeared in Uganda in 1999 and has spread toward Asia's breadbaskets.

climax.text: Breeding rust-resistant wheat is a constant arms race—new resistance genes are overcome within years.

punchline.text: Fungi evolve to beat resistance as fast as we create it.

quiz.question: What percentage of plant diseases are caused by fungi?

details.summary: Fungal diseases are responsible for the largest share of plant disease losses globally, destroying an estimated 10-23% of crops annually. This topic covers major fungal pathogens like rusts, blights, and molds, how they spread, and why they are so difficult to control.
details.whyItMatters: Fungal crop diseases destroy enough food to feed 600 million people each year. Emerging fungal threats are increasing due to climate change, pesticide resistance, and global trade in infected plant material.
takeaways: Fungi cause 70-80% of all plant diseases and destroy 10-23% of global crops
Spores spread through wind, water, soil, and infected seeds over vast distances
Major fungal diseases include wheat rust, rice blast, and potato late blight

faq.question: What makes fungal diseases so destructive to crops?
faq.answer: Fungi produce millions of microscopic spores that travel on wind and water across continents. They can survive dormant in soil for years, infect plants through any surface, and evolve rapidly to overcome resistant varieties. Many produce toxins dangerous to human health.

faq.question: Which fungal diseases pose the greatest threat to global food security?
faq.answer: Wheat stem rust (especially strain Ug99) threatens global wheat production. Rice blast destroys enough rice to feed 60 million people annually. Fusarium wilt threatens banana production worldwide. Panama disease could potentially devastate the Cavendish banana industry.
